description.text: The promos of the HeartGold & SoulSilver Series, HGSS01 to HGSS25, released from February 2010 to February 2011, when the promo prefix changed from DP to HGSS. Ho-Oh and Lugia came in poster packs and the Knock Out Collection; the Johto first partners in spring 2010 collector's tins and the legendary beasts Raikou, Entei and Suicune in the fall tins; the rest in blisters of each expansion through Call of Legends. Latias and Latios came both in cosmos holo and in cracked ice holo, and the trophy card Tropical Tidal Wave went to players at the 2010 World Championships.

tell.text: A black star promo symbol and an "HGSS" number at the bottom right

description.text:
A holofoil Ho-Oh from one of the two HeartGold & SoulSilver poster packs of February 2010, each with two HeartGold & SoulSilver booster packs, two POP Series 9 packs and a double-sided poster. The other pack held Lugia HGSS02: it was the first time a single set had more than one poster pack. Both promos came back later in the HeartGold & SoulSilver Knock Out Collection, a box of three booster packs sold only at Rite Aid pharmacies near the end of the series.

Takashi Yamaguchi's art first came in Japan as Ho-Oh 048/L-P, given to players in the first qualifying stage of the 2010 tournament that chose Japan's World Championships representatives.

A holofoil Lugia from one of the two HeartGold & SoulSilver poster packs of February 2010, each with two HeartGold & SoulSilver booster packs, two POP Series 9 packs and a double-sided poster. The other pack held Ho-Oh HGSS01: it was the first time a single set had more than one poster pack. Both promos came back later in the HeartGold & SoulSilver Knock Out Collection, a box of three booster packs sold only at Rite Aid pharmacies near the end of the series.

Takashi Yamaguchi's art first came in Japan as Lugia 047/L-P, given to players in the first qualifying stage of the 2010 tournament that chose Japan's World Championships representatives.

A holofoil Pikachu from the HeartGold & SoulSilver three-pack blister, released with the set on 10 February 2010 with two HeartGold & SoulSilver booster packs, one Legends Awakened pack and a coin. The other blister held Wobbuffet HGSS04. Pikachu came back once the Black & White series had begun, in the HeartGold & SoulSilver Variety Blister, which held three random older booster packs.

Kanako Eo's art first came in Japan as a Gold Rank prize of the Pokémon Daisuki Club, for members who had collected 1,200 Action Points: first as 016/DPt-P, then reprinted as 019/L-P when the card game moved into the LEGEND era. Its Weakness reads +10 instead of ×2, making it the only HeartGold & SoulSilver series card with an added-damage Weakness and the last new English card to have one.

A holofoil Wobbuffet from the HeartGold & SoulSilver three-pack blister, released with the set on 10 February 2010 with two HeartGold & SoulSilver booster packs, one Legends Awakened pack and a coin. The other blister held Pikachu HGSS03.

The art, by match, first came in Japan as Wobbuffet 040/L-P, given to players at the Challenge Hiroba tournaments of November 2009.

A holofoil Hoothoot from the HeartGold & SoulSilver two-pack blister, which held both Hoothoot and Noctowl HGSS06 with one HeartGold & SoulSilver booster pack and one POP Series 9 pack. The blister turned up early at Target stores in the first days of February 2010, before the set's release on 10 February. When the pair surfaced, PokéBeach noted that the black star promos had started again from 1 with an HGSS prefix in place of DP.

Masakazu Fukuda's art first came in Japan as Hoothoot 025/L-P, given to players at the Knockout Battle events of the Pokémon Battle Challenge, held around Japan between October and December 2009.

A holofoil Noctowl from the HeartGold & SoulSilver two-pack blister, which held both Hoothoot HGSS05 and Noctowl with one HeartGold & SoulSilver booster pack and one POP Series 9 pack. The blister turned up early at Target stores in the first days of February 2010, before the set's release on 10 February.

Masakazu Fukuda's art first came in Japan as Noctowl 026/L-P, given to players who won at least one battle at the Knockout Battle events of the Pokémon Battle Challenge, held around Japan between October and December 2009.

A holofoil Feraligatr from the 2010 spring Collector's Tins, sold from February 2010 with two HeartGold & SoulSilver booster packs, one Platinum pack and one Diamond & Pearl series pack. The other tins held Meganium HGSS08 and Typhlosion HGSS09, the final forms of the three Johto starter Pokémon.

It reprints the Pokémon Prime Feraligatr of HeartGold & SoulSilver (108/123) with a new drawing by the same artist, Kent Kanetsuna, made for the English tins. The set's own card came from Japan's HeartGold Collection.

A holofoil Meganium from the 2010 spring Collector's Tins, sold from February 2010 with two HeartGold & SoulSilver booster packs, one Platinum pack and one Diamond & Pearl series pack. The other tins held Feraligatr HGSS07 and Typhlosion HGSS09, the final forms of the three Johto starter Pokémon.

It reprints the Pokémon Prime Meganium of HeartGold & SoulSilver (109/123), drawn by Takashi Yamaguchi, with a new drawing by Noriko Hotta made for the English tins. The set's own card came from Japan's SoulSilver Collection.

A holofoil Typhlosion from the 2010 spring Collector's Tins, sold from February 2010 with two HeartGold & SoulSilver booster packs, one Platinum pack and one Diamond & Pearl series pack. The other tins held Feraligatr HGSS07 and Meganium HGSS08, the final forms of the three Johto starter Pokémon.

It reprints the Pokémon Prime Typhlosion of HeartGold & SoulSilver (110/123) with a new drawing by the same artist, Wataru Kawahara, made for the English tins. The set's own card came from Japan's SoulSilver Collection.

A holofoil Latias from the Unleashed three-pack blister, released with Unleashed on 12 May 2010 with two Unleashed booster packs, one Stormfront pack and a coin. The other blister held Latios HGSS11, and the two cards' art joins into one picture when they sit side by side. At first the blisters were on sale only outside America.

Wataru Kawahara's art first came in Japan as Latias 045/L-P, which came with Latios in both the HeartGold Collection and the SoulSilver Collection special packs of 1 January 2010.

A holofoil Cleffa from the Unleashed two-pack blister of May 2010, which held both Cleffa and Smoochum HGSS13 with one Unleashed booster pack and one POP Series 9 pack, sold at stores such as Wal-Mart and Target. Both promos are holofoil reprints of rares from HeartGold & SoulSilver.

It reprints HeartGold & SoulSilver's Cleffa (17/123) and Masakazu Fukuda's art, which first came in Japan's HeartGold Collection. Call of Legends later reprinted the card again with new art by sui.

A holofoil Smoochum from the Unleashed two-pack blister of May 2010, which held both Cleffa HGSS12 and Smoochum with one Unleashed booster pack and one POP Series 9 pack, sold at stores such as Wal-Mart and Target. Both promos are holofoil reprints of rares from HeartGold & SoulSilver.

It reprints HeartGold & SoulSilver's Smoochum (30/123) and Midori Harada's art, which first came in Japan's HeartGold Collection.

A holofoil Lapras from the Undaunted three-pack blister, released with Undaunted on 18 August 2010 with two Undaunted booster packs, one Arceus pack and a coin showing Chikorita, Cyndaquil or Totodile. The other blister held Shuckle HGSS15.

Masakazu Fukuda's art first came in Japan as Lapras 058/L-P, a prize at the Challenge Hiroba tournaments of May 2010.

A holofoil Shuckle from the Undaunted three-pack blister, released with Undaunted on 18 August 2010 with two Undaunted booster packs, one Arceus pack and a coin showing Chikorita, Cyndaquil or Totodile. The other blister held Lapras HGSS14.

The art, by match, first came in Japan as Shuckle 067/L-P, given to players at the Challenge Hiroba tournaments of June 2010.

A cracked ice holofoil Plusle from the Undaunted two-pack blister of August 2010, which held both Plusle and Minun HGSS17 with one Undaunted booster pack and one POP Series 9 pack, sold at stores such as Wal-Mart and Target.

It reprints Unleashed's Plusle (number 36) in cracked ice holofoil. Kouki Saitou's art first came in Japan in the Raichu deck of the Battle Starter Decks.

A cracked ice holofoil Minun from the Undaunted two-pack blister of August 2010, which held both Plusle HGSS16 and Minun with one Undaunted booster pack and one POP Series 9 pack, sold at stores such as Wal-Mart and Target.

It reprints Unleashed's Minun (number 34) in cracked ice holofoil. Kouki Saitou's art first came in Japan in the Raichu deck of the Battle Starter Decks.

Tropical Tidal Wave was the promo card of the 2010 Pokémon World Championships, held from 13 to 15 August 2010 at the Hilton Waikoloa Village in Hawaii. Competitors received the card in seven languages and staff got a Staff copy. The trophy versions carry a placement stamp from Top Thirty-Two up to Finalist; Champion copies only began in 2012.

tell.text: "FINALIST" printed below the card text, with the World Championships stamp on the picture: a prize for that placing.
"QUARTER-FINALIST" printed below the card text, with the World Championships stamp on the picture: a prize for that placing.
"SEMI-FINALIST" printed below the card text, with the World Championships stamp on the picture: a prize for that placing.
"STAFF" printed on the card, with the World Championships stamp on the picture: for the people who ran the event.

description.text: The stamped staff copy, given to those who helped run the 2010 World Championships. Other stamped copies went to the top players in each division.

tell.text: "TOP SIXTEEN" printed below the card text, with the World Championships stamp on the picture: a prize for that placing.
"TOP THIRTY-TWO" printed below the card text, with the World Championships stamp on the picture: a prize for that placing.
A World Championships stamp on the picture: "Worlds" and the year on early cards, the World Championships logo and year on later ones.

description.text: The 2010 Tropical Tidal Wave, given to every player of the trading card game at the start of the 2010 World Championships, in a nine-card collection: the card in seven languages, a card advertising the next World Championship Decks and one with the date and venue of the next World Championships.

A holofoil Raikou in its shiny colors from the 2010 fall Collector's Tins, sold from September 2010. Each tin held its shiny promo, a cracked ice holofoil reprint of the same Pokémon's Secret Wonders card to show the difference, and one pack each of Undaunted, HeartGold & SoulSilver, the Platinum series and the Diamond & Pearl series. The other tins held Entei HGSS20 and Suicune HGSS21, and a note inside promised more shiny Pokémon in future sets.

Noriko Hotta's art first came in Japan as Raikou 061/L-P in the LEGEND Perfect Set, released with the film Zoroark: Master of Illusions on 10 July 2010. The card matches the shiny Raikou that Japanese players could get for their games as a promotion for the film: its only attack, Zap Cannon, is the special move that Raikou knew.

The other tins held Raikou HGSS19 and Suicune HGSS21, and a note inside promised more shiny Pokémon in future sets.

The card matches the shiny Entei that Japanese players could get for their games as a promotion for the film: its only attack, Flare Blitz, is the special move that Entei knew.

Each tin held its shiny promo, a cracked ice holofoil reprint of the same Pokémon's Secret Wonders card to show the difference, and one pack each of Undaunted, HeartGold & SoulSilver, the Platinum series and the Diamond & Pearl series. The other tins held Raikou HGSS19 and Entei HGSS20, and a note inside promised more shiny Pokémon in future sets.

The card matches the shiny Suicune that Japanese players could get for their games as a promotion for the film: its only attack, Sheer Cold, is the special move that Suicune knew.

A holofoil Porygon from the Triumphant three-pack blister, released with Triumphant on 2 November 2010 with two Triumphant booster packs, one Platinum pack and a coin. Porygon2 HGSS23 also came in the Triumphant blisters, and the two cards' art joins into one picture side by side.

TOKIYA's art first came in Japan as Porygon 077/L-P, from the Summer Battle Campaign of August 2010: players collected stamps on a points card by playing at Gym Challenge venues or buying LEGEND booster packs, and five stamps earned Porygon. The Japanese print carries the Gym Challenge logo, which the English one drops.

A holofoil Porygon2 from the Triumphant three-pack blister, released with Triumphant on 2 November 2010 with two Triumphant booster packs, one Platinum pack and a coin. Porygon HGSS22 also came in the Triumphant blisters, and the two cards' art joins into one picture side by side.

TOKIYA's art first came in Japan as Porygon2 078/L-P, from the Summer Battle Campaign of August 2010: players collected stamps on a points card by playing at Gym Challenge venues or buying LEGEND booster packs, and fifteen stamps earned Porygon2. The Japanese print carries the Gym Challenge logo, which the English one drops.

A cracked ice holofoil Hitmonchan from the Call of Legends three-pack blister, released with Call of Legends in February 2011 with two Call of Legends booster packs, one HeartGold & SoulSilver pack and a coin. The other blister held Hitmonlee HGSS25.

It reprints Undaunted's Hitmonchan (number 51) in cracked ice holofoil, with Kouki Saitou's art from Japan's Tyranitar Constructed Standard Deck. Call of Legends itself reprinted the card with a new drawing by the same artist.
